title: Forecast Reliability, Resolution and Decision Value
purpose: Separate probability reliability from resolution and assess decision value under explicit preparedness cost/loss profiles, including human-review deferral, across the same stratified rare-event regimes.
scope_limits: All forecast outcomes, costs, decision profiles and human-review fallback actions are fictional public-development data.
The scenario/forecast cases are re-used from NRES-010; this is a linked evaluation increment, not independent validation data.
Importance weights apply only to the declared target/proposal stratum mixture and representative within-stratum cases.
All loss and cost parameters are normalized synthetic planning units, not currency or real operational budgets.
The benchmark evaluates abstract preparedness choices; it is not an emergency procedure, resource allocation instruction or legally authorized operational plan.
A forecast that is calibrated but has no resolution may have little decision value; decision value depends on cost/loss profiles.
Abstentions trigger a separately authored review fallback and explicit deferral cost; those fallback decisions are evaluator-owned reference inputs, not model outputs.
The public fixture cannot establish causal effectiveness or real-world savings.

source_fixture.source_description: The 128 public synthetic NRES-010 forecast/observation cases are preserved with stable source_case_id values, regime IDs and importance-sampling metadata.

sampling_design.design_note: 24 routine and 8 tail-enriched cases per regime; estimates target the declared 97%/3% stratum mixture only if cases are representative within their respective strata.

calibration_reference.description: Fictional historical training cohort used only to construct a fixed climatology comparison. It is not a real event base rate.

protocol.bin_convention: lower-inclusive and upper-exclusive; final bin includes 1.0
protocol.brier_decomposition: weighted fixed-bin Murphy decomposition of the coarsened forecast: reliability minus resolution plus uncertainty; report original unbinned Brier and finite-bin residual separately
protocol.decision_rule: prepare when predicted exceedance probability is greater than or equal to readiness_cost/(event_loss_without_action-event_loss_with_action)
protocol.decision_cost: prepare: readiness_cost + event*event_loss_with_action; no_action: event*event_loss_without_action; add deferral_cost for an abstention routed to review_fallback_action
protocol.value_rule: relative_economic_value=(training_climatology_policy_cost-candidate_policy_cost)/(training_climatology_policy_cost-perfect_information_oracle_cost), report denominator and undefined state if non-positive
protocol.abstention_rule: missing or conflicting source inputs require abstention; score the separately supplied reviewer fallback action plus deferral cost
protocol.aggregation_rule: report each profile and regime separately; never aggregate different user cost/loss profiles into one score

interpretation_guardrails: Forecast probabilities and evaluator observations are separate fields.
The fixed training climatology action is derived only from the declared calibration-reference probability, not from public test outcomes.
Perfect-information oracle is an unattainable lower-bound comparator and must never be presented as an achievable policy.
The reviewer fallback action is an evaluator-owned human-review reference, not a candidate model decision.
A higher relative economic value is meaningful only within the exact declared cost/loss profile and sampling design.
Report reliability, resolution, uncertainty, original Brier and finite-bin decomposition residual independently.
Finite-bin reliability/resolution components are descriptive estimates and can be biased at small sample sizes.
Importance-weighted policy loss and effective sample size must be reported for every profile and regime.
Abstention coverage and deferral costs cannot be omitted.
No composite resilience, political, loyalty, enlistment or personal-suitability score is permitted.
